questions.prompt: Match each component to its job.

pairs.right: Holds data the computer is using right now
Keeps files when the power is off
Converts AC mains power to DC for the parts

questions.explanation: Knowing what each part does is the starting point for troubleshooting.

questions.prompt: Which statement about RAM is true?
choices: It keeps Windows installed when the computer is off
It is volatile: its contents are lost when power is removed
It is slower than a hard disk drive
Any RAM module fits any motherboard
questions.explanation: RAM is fast, temporary memory. DDR generations are not interchangeable.

questions.prompt: A computer has a dedicated graphics card. Where should the monitor be connected?
choices: To the graphics card's video port
questions.explanation: Most motherboards turn off their own video output when a dedicated card is installed.

questions.prompt: Which of these are types of storage? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A DIMM is a RAM module and a PSU supplies power; neither stores files.

questions.prompt: Which connector supplies power to the motherboard itself?
questions.explanation: The 24-pin ATX connector powers the motherboard; the separate 4+4-pin EPS connector powers the CPU.
